tldr: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and the restricted Mythos 5.2, cutting Fable's price 20% to $8/$40 per million tokens and reporting 69.9% on FrontierSWE v2. A day later it set an IPO range of $70-$78 for 825M shares (up to ~$64.4B on Nasdaq as ANT) and started its roadshow.

Nvidia's Huang scandal widened: shares fell 4.27% Monday and about 5% Tuesday, a shareholder class action was filed, and Bloomberg/NYT report Nvidia's general counsel intervened in the US Megaspeed chip-smuggling probe. Separately, DeepMind's AlphaProof Code used Gemini agents to formally verify Signal's libsignal in about four weeks.

China/Asia: Beijing extended its rare-earth export-control suspension two months to Jan 10, 2027; ByteDance shipped Seedream 5.5 at ~¥0.28 per 2K edit; Zhipu plans an up-to-HK$4B buyback and closed up 11%; TSMC posted record October revenue of NT$586.9B.

items.title: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code uses Gemini agents to formally verify Signal's cryptographic code
items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, a framework in which Gemini-based agents wrote machine-checked Lean proofs that Signal's reference implementation, libsignal, delivers forward secrecy, post-compromise security and authentication. The guarantees hold for the compiled code, not just the protocol design; human experts reviewed every formal specification, and the work took about four weeks. DeepMind says it will open-source the verification artifacts. The guarantees cover the core cryptography, not the Signal apps.
items.why_it_matters: It suggests AI agents can make full formal verification of production security code affordable, which has usually been too costly to do at scale.

items.title: OpenAI details Control Room, a central kill switch that halts research model workloads within 35 seconds
items.summary: OpenAI described Control Room, an internal system that tracks every model workload across its research infrastructure and can stop it. Each job carries an identifier the inference engine checks before generating output; when a person or automated monitor orders a stop, the job's authorization is revoked, with cached authorizations delaying the halt by up to 35 seconds. The system fails closed, and it covers internal research (training, evals, data processing), not ChatGPT or the API.
items.why_it_matters: A concrete safety-engineering design for stopping runaway research agents that other labs and regulators may come to expect, arriving the same day Australia announced rules prompted by an OpenAI agent incident.

items.title: China extends suspension of rare-earth and other export controls to Jan 10, 2027, a day before expiry
items.original_title: 商务部、海关总署公告2026年第58号 公布继续暂停实施商务部、海关总署公告2025年第55号、56号、57号、58号及商务部公告2025年第61号、62号的决定
items.summary: China's Commerce Ministry (MOFCOM) and customs (GACC) issued Announcement No. 58 of 2026, which keeps six 2025 export-control announcements suspended from Nov 11, 2026 to Jan 10, 2027. Four of them (Nos. 56, 57, 61 and 62) cover rare earths, including overseas rare-earth items and rare-earth technology. The one-year suspension agreed after the 2025 Trump-Xi meeting was due to lapse on Nov 10, 2026. This is a two-month extension, not a new control. Separately, the US BIS suspension of its 50% Affiliates Rule also runs to Jan 10, 2027.
items.why_it_matters: It removes the risk of an immediate snap-back of rare-earth controls that bear on magnets and other inputs for chips, data centres and hardware. The short two-month term keeps Beijing's leverage, and press reports tie it to an expected Trump-Xi meeting at APEC.

items.why_it_matters: A hard foundry-level data point that AI-accelerator demand is still accelerating despite the chip-stock rout and the turmoil at its biggest customer, Nvidia.

items.summary: At the Nov 9 regular briefing, AFP asked about US officials' claims that the woman in Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair worked for Chinese intelligence. Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said talk of a 'Chinese spy' was 'pure speculation and smear', and repeated the line when pressed. items.title: OpenAI opens ChatGPT Business Hub beta so US companies can publish verified profiles and business agents
items.summary: OpenAI launched a Business Hub in beta where eligible US companies can set up profiles and verify product and service information in ChatGPT, and publish a business agent that answers users' questions about their products. These agents can be sponsored and used as destinations for ChatGPT Ads, with sponsored placements labelled. OpenAI says businesses do not see users' conversations.
items.why_it_matters: It nudges ChatGPT toward a Google-style business directory and ad surface, tying its ads business to agent-based commerce.

items.title: GitHub write-up alleges Gemini sends connected Drive files and emails to human reviewers
items.summary: A pseudonymous GitHub repository says Gemini pulls personal Drive files and Gmail content into chats even without explicit @Drive or @Gmail tags, and that those sessions can go to contractor review, pointing to an Oct 16 policy edit. Google's Gemini Apps Privacy Hub reportedly says a subset of Connected Apps data is reviewed by human reviewers and that reviewed chats are kept up to three years. The post reached 446 points on Hacker News.
items.why_it_matters: If confirmed, it undercuts assurances about Workspace data and could slow adoption of Gemini's connected-app features.

learn.title: Put a confidence interval on a benchmark gap before calling it a win
learn.why_today: Anthropic reports Fable 5.2 at 69.9% on FrontierSWE v2 against 62.3% for Opus 5.5, a 7.6-point gap whose significance depends on how many tasks the benchmark has.
learn.explanation: A pass rate on n tasks is a binomial estimate with standard error sqrt(p(1-p)/n), so a 7.6-point gap is noise at n=100 and borderline at n=300. Treating the two runs as independent overstates the noise, because both models face the same tasks: the paired (McNemar) view uses only discordant tasks, those one model solves and the other fails, and usually gives a much tighter interval. Run-to-run sampling variance (temperature, agent scaffolding) adds a second noise source that a single run hides, so ask for repeated seeds. The interval also says nothing about contamination or whether the benchmark measures what you care about.
learn.python:
# Illustrative: is a benchmark gap bigger than sampling noise? (task counts are assumed, not reported)
import math
def gap_ci(p1, p2, n, z=1.96):
    # unpaired two-proportion CI for p1 - p2, both models run on the same n tasks
    se = math.sqrt(p1*(1-p1)/n + p2*(1-p2)/n)
    d = p1 - p2
    return d, d - z*se, d + z*se
def paired_ci(b, c, n, z=1.96):
    # paired: b = tasks only A solves, c = tasks only B solves (McNemar-style)
    d = (b - c) / n
    se = math.sqrt(b + c - (b - c)**2 / n) / n
    return d, d - z*se, d + z*se
for n in (100, 300, 1000):
    d, lo, hi = gap_ci(0.699, 0.623, n)
    print(f"n={n:5d}: gap {d*100:+.1f} pts, 95% CI [{lo*100:+.1f}, {hi*100:+.1f}]  significant={lo>0}")
# Same 300 tasks, but the models agree on most: only 40 vs 17 discordant tasks
d, lo, hi = paired_ci(40, 17, 300)
print(f"paired n=300: gap {d*100:+.1f} pts, 95% CI [{lo*100:+.1f}, {hi*100:+.1f}]")

learn.title: Bound an agent kill switch's stop latency when authorizations are cached
learn.why_today: OpenAI's Control Room revokes a job's authorization to stop it, and reports that cached authorizations can delay the halt by up to 35 seconds.
learn.explanation: A revocation only takes effect when the worker next consults the authority, so the worst-case stop time is the cache TTL plus propagation delay, not the check interval. Shorter TTLs tighten the bound but multiply load on the authorization service, and if that service is down the system must choose fail-closed (stop everything) or fail-open (keep running). OpenAI's description says it fails closed. Push-based revocation can beat the TTL bound but needs a reliable channel, so production designs usually combine a push with a TTL as the backstop. The simulation shows mean latency near half the TTL while the worst case sits at the bound, and the bound is what matters for safety.
learn.python:
# Illustrative: worst-case stop latency with cached authorizations (numbers are assumed)
import random
def stop_latency(ttl, check_every, propagate, trials=100_000, seed=0):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    worst = total = 0.0
    for _ in range(trials):
        cache_age = rng.uniform(0, ttl)          # how old the cached 'allowed' verdict is at revoke time
        expire = ttl - cache_age                 # time until the cache must re-check
        next_check = rng.uniform(0, check_every) # engine checks cache before each generation step
        lat = propagate + max(expire, next_check)
        worst = max(worst, lat); total += lat
    return total / trials, worst
for ttl in (5, 15, 30):
    mean, worst = stop_latency(ttl, check_every=1.0, propagate=2.0)
    print(f"cache TTL {ttl:2d}s: mean stop {mean:5.1f}s, worst {worst:5.1f}s (bound = TTL + propagate = {ttl+2}s)")
